result.title: SpeCal: Spectral Calibration for Unsupervised RLVR
result.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved the reasoning abilities of large language models, but its dependence on ground-truth answers or external verifiers limits its ability to exploit abundant unlabeled reasoning data. Unsupervised RLVR alleviates this bottleneck by deriving scalar rewards from the model's own rollouts. However, the reliability of such self-generated supervision varies substantially across rollout groups and individual responses, while existing methods construct or refine their rewards mainly from decoded outcomes and reward statistics. These endpoint signals reveal what answers the model produces, but provide limited information about whether the underlying rollout representations form a reliable structure for learning. Our key observation is that hidden-state spectra offer a complementary view of supervision reliability by characterizing both the organization of a rollout group and the support received by each rollout within that group. Based on this observation, we propose SpeCal, a bi-level spectral calibration framework for unsupervised RLVR. At the group level, SpeCal combines spectral mass with a Gaussian band-pass gate over normalized entropy-based effective rank, favoring rollout groups with substantial representation variation whose effective dimensionality lies in a preferred regime. At the rollout level, the same group effective rank determines how many dominant directions are retained in a leave-one-out spectral subspace formed by the remaining rollouts, within which the conditional support of each held-out rollout is measured. The resulting signals calibrate the original reward-induced advantages at the group and rollout levels without redefining the underlying unlabeled reward.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SpeCal，从 rollout 隐藏状态谱的组级有效秩与组内留一子空间支持两方面校准无监督 RLVR 的奖励优势，以提升自生成监督的可靠性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其谱有效秩和留一子空间支持为衡量 latent 状态的结构可靠性与单条轨迹贡献提供了可核查线索，可能启发 LVR 中的轨迹贡献分配与监督筛选；但属纯文本训练方法，需确认向多模态 latent 推理的迁移性。
